{
  "cvss_vector": "CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:L/SA:N",
  "aivss": { "LC": "D", "CP": "S", "AP": "C", "RH": "N", "ES": "W" },
  "rationales": {
    "LC": "The attacker sends a JSON-RPC tools/call register_tool request whose name and description text reach the tool registry unvalidated, with no enforced transformation before the sink.",
    "CP": "The replaced registry entry persists in the PluginBot server process beyond the registering request, but is in-process state lost when the process stops, not a durable store.",
    "AP": "The effect is confined to PluginBot's own tool registry and its advertised description; no trust boundary into another principal or agent is crossed.",
    "RH": "No evaluator, verifier, or reward channel exists on this path; the attack replaces a tool listing entry, and no proxy-objective surface is reachable.",
    "ES": "PluginBot accepts run-time tool registrations with no signature or source check, an unvetted dynamic extension surface."
  },
  "evidence": {
    "LC": [
      "A JSON-RPC tools/call request that registers a tool under an existing tool's name. No authentication.",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:738-785",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:2159-2251"
    ],
    "CP": [
      "register_tool adds or replaces an entry in the advertised tool list (up to 16).",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:2159-2251",
      "As documented: all later calls to that name route to the attacker's version, which returns modified or malicious results."
    ],
    "AP": [
      "MCP tool server that accepts tool registrations with no verification. (PluginBot role)",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:2159-2251",
      "As implemented, the advertised description of the tool is replaced."
    ],
    "RH": [
      "PluginBot register_tool, store_secret, fetch_data — capability write, read — register_tool adds or replaces an entry in the advertised tool list; a registered tool gets no new handler.",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/agent-success-paths.js:113-156"
    ],
    "ES": [
      "PluginBot accepts new tool definitions at run time with no signature or source check.",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:747-752",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1915-1926"
    ]
  },
  "confidence": { "LC": "high", "CP": "medium", "AP": "high", "RH": "medium", "ES": "high" },
  "rh_facts": {
    "reachable_proxy": false,
    "isolation_verified": false,
    "verified_episodes": 0,
    "episodes_reviewed": 0,
    "locus": null
  },
  "automatable": "Yes",
  "automatable_rationale": "The attack is a pair of unauthenticated JSON-RPC requests (list then register) covered by an automated unit test that runs without a fleet; no human interaction is required.",
  "technical_impact": "Partial",
  "technical_impact_rationale": "As implemented by default the registration replaces only the advertised description while the original handler is kept, so calls still execute the real tool; full interception described in the documentation is not the default behavior.",
  "applicability_as_implemented": {
    "model_directed_goal_pursuit": false,
    "selects_or_sequences_actions": false,
    "rationale": "In the default simulated configuration no model is called and PluginBot is a tool server whose handlers are fixed code; tool registration only edits a listing entry."
  },
  "applicability_as_modeled": {
    "model_directed_goal_pursuit": false,
    "selects_or_sequences_actions": false,
    "rationale": "Even in optional LLM mode no tools are passed to the model and scripted handlers execute all behavior, so the agent never selects or sequences tool actions."
  },
  "refusal": null
}
message.reasoning:
Assess: MCP tool registration shadowing on PluginBot. Entry is JSON-RPC tools/call — structured, not natural language. But registration includes description text — attacker-supplied description. LC: direct? The attacker-supplied tool registration content (name/description) is structured fields but registration accepts natural language description without validation — Direct (attacker-supplied language reaches registry unmediated). I'd say LC=D.

CP: registration persists in registry across requests (process lifetime) — but is that "memory"? CP: registration persists in the tool registry within a server process — durable? Registry persists within process, not cross-session durable store. Could be S (session context) or N. The registry entry persists beyond a session — but it's not a memory store. Rubric CP concerns attacker-controlled context/memory persistence; registry entry replacement persists across sessions within process. I'll say CP=N (stateless requests; no memory carryover... but the registry persists). Hmm — the registration changes standing advertised tool list. That's like standing behavior. I'd say CP=S (ephemeral in-process state, lost when process stops) or N. The rubric S is "ephemeral session state (conversation buffer...) unreachable after session boundary". Registry entry persists past session. C requires durable stores (vector DB etc.). Registry isn't a memory store; I'll go N? Actually attacker-controlled context persisting beyond request... The registry is not "memory/context" in the LLM sense but it's standing state. Given the rubric letter C targets memory stores, and S targets session-only, this is in-process cross-request — closest to N? I'll pick S with rationale, or X. I'll go with S? Hmm. Actually let me pick CP=N with note single-turn/stateless; but that's wrong since registration persists. Safer: CP=S, medium confidence? The registry persists across sessions though. I'll go X... Better decide: rubric says "Stored source content that is only re-retrieved... is not CP". Tool description change alters standing advertised behavior — that's closer to persistent standing behavior. But not in a durable store. I'll choose S.

AP: same agent component, no trust boundary crossed → C (contained).

RH: no evaluator/reward channel here → N? RH N requires test confirming isolation of evaluator channels. There's no evaluator on path; verified_episodes 0, isolation not specifically tested → P? No evaluator reachable... RH: no proxy objective on path. Rubric N requires test confirming isolation. No test. Hmm. P is "agent can reach a proxy objective... on the path" — there's none. N needs test. I'll say N with low confidence? Default to N: no reward/evaluator channel exists on this path at all, so None (or X). I'll pick N with low confidence.

ES: PluginBot accepts unvetted dynamic tool registrations, no verification → W.

CVSS: AV:N (network, though default binds loopback; documented Docker binds 127.0.0.1... docker-compose publishes on 127.0.0.1, so AV:L? Attacker needs network access to MCP port; precondition "network access to the MCP port". Default bind is loopback → adjacent? CVSS for lab default: local. AV:L. AC:L, AT:N, PR:N, UI:N. Vulnerable system = agent application. Impact: VC? tool description replacement, no data modified per implementation... As documented it intercepts all calls → integrity impact on subsequent systems. Score as implemented default: registration replaces advertised description; handler unchanged. Impact: VI low on agent? Subsequent callers get changed description → SI:L. I'll give VC:N/VI:L(agent)/VA:N, SC:N/SI:L/SA:N.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:L/SA:N

AIVSS: LC=D, CP=S, AP=C, RH=N, ES=W. Severity: LC direct → attacker control? Lookup A: with RH none... A0/A1 classification: LC=D gives High control presumably. Not needed to compute score, just letters.

automatable: Yes (automated JSON-RPC calls, no human).
technical_impact: Partial (description replaced, handler kept).

applicability: no model in default; modeled also deterministic/scripted — model_directed_goal_pursuit false both.
